㊥ (committed and pushed) I've updated M-象-2000, committed it as futon3c `964fa778` and pushed futon3c master to GitHub. The push also carried the four commits from the evidence fixes: `3bd7b7fd`, `c182dfa1`, `e44ccd34` and `8ec734fa`. futon3c master is now level with origin. Today's futon2 commits, the mark-act alignment work and codex-10's acts-file edit, were already on `origin/main`, so futon2 had nothing to push.

㊢ (what the M-象-2000 update says) I added three entries at the end of INSTANTIATE, just before DOCUMENT:
- **The agreement on codex-10's offer.** Your "Yes" couldn't be checked, for three reasons:
  - the evidence chain was broken for 17 hours, and I replayed it;
  - user turns replied to the commits record instead of the agent's chat turn;
  - codex seats recorded their turns under the author `codex` instead of the seat id.
  
  The entry gives each fix's commit, and two things still outstanding:
  - the offer was marked ㊮, not 🈸, so it still won't be read as an offer;
  - the fixes take effect only after you reload `agent-chat.el` and `codex-repl.el`.
- **The late withdrawal notice in codex-17's buffer.** It is recorded as found but not fixed, with the proposed fix of quoting the fragment in the notice line.
- **A pointer to the mark-act alignment in futon2.**

previous_reply_acts.text:
(timeline from 象's record `~/.emacs-graph/session-turn-analysis/turn-GYGJ2e.json`)
- 14:43:13: your turn 21, "You don't need to cancel, just do what I asked".
- 14:46:07: the analysis came back. "You don't need to cancel" was read as withdraw with `target null`. Its stated reason: the thing cancelled "is not named as an act id in the turn, so the target is left null rather than guessed". "just do what I asked" was read as continue.
- 14:47:09: the notice was shown in the buffer. The withdrawal post was answered `422 target-unresolved`. A negation interpretation was stored as `interpretation-negation:b53d095d…`, with resolution `target-unresolved`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what's wrong with how it showed up) The reading itself looks right to me, and recording no target rather than guessing one is what's supposed to happen. The fault is in the display. The notice is inserted at the prompt whenever the analysis finishes, and it doesn't say which turn it belongs to. With a three-minute analysis, it can land under a later exchange, as it did here. Quoting the fragment in the line, e.g. `withdraw inferred on "You don't need to cancel": unresolved (no target)`, would be a small fix. I haven't sent that one out. Say if you want it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the bells)
- **Fix 1, codex-16:** a failed evidence record must not take the rest of the session down with it. The test plants a predecessor in `failed/` and checks that the next record still drains. Job `invoke-1790952744854-30384-e78c5dcb`, park `park-c62ef2ff-0ea7-4a91-82bb-eb3d81b33c58`; it's running.
- **Fix 3, kimi-2:** codex-repl should record its turns under the seat id rather than `codex`. kimi-2 first checks for consumers that select evidence by author `codex`, and stops if any would break. Job `invoke-1790952783868-30386-af3f9e02`, park `park-5045088d-6c41-461f-bb72-51fe48b5e4c4`; it's running. I first sent this to zai-5, which refused it with `429`: its weekly limit is exhausted until 2026-10-06 10:04.
- **Fix 2:** user turns should reply to the agent's last chat turn, not its turn-commits record. It's queued in fix 1's wake checklist, to go to codex-16 when fix 1 lands.
